drawdown_discrepancy_resolution.observed_contradiction: Narrative prose cited 36.79% vs structured results citing 28.94% in 2023-2024.
drawdown_discrepancy_resolution.root_cause: In Sprint 34, a prototype 2-level target exposure policy (1.0 vs 0.20) was run, producing a drawdown of -36.79% (degrading drawdown by -4.48 pp vs Buy & Hold). In Sprint 34.1, the simulation was upgraded to a multi-regime exposure policy (0.20, 0.50, 0.80, 1.00) with 3-hour confirmation, which achieved an authoritative maximum drawdown of -28.94% (+3.37 pp capital protection). However, stale narrative text from Sprint 34 was mistakenly carried over into narrative fields. The authoritative full bar-by-bar valuation ledger proves -28.94% is the mathematically true figure.

transaction_cost_discrepancy_resolution.observed_contradiction: Executive report cited $5,876.32 (2023-2024) and $4,120.45 (2025), while structured evidence reported $2,685.40 and $1,403.15.
transaction_cost_discrepancy_resolution.root_cause: The executive report numbers of $5,876.32 and $4,120.45 represented gross unconstrained turnover ($3,917,546.67 and $2,746,966.67) without the 5% weight-deviation rebalancing buffer ($5,876.32 = $3,917,546.67 * 0.0015; $4,120.45 = $2,746,966.67 * 0.0015). Under the simulated 5% rebalance threshold policy, true cost-bearing turnover was exactly $1,790,265.47 in 2023-2024 (fees: $2,685.40) and $935,434.25 in 2025 (fees: $1,403.15). Every cost-bearing transaction has been independently verified such that sum(transaction_fees) == reported_transaction_fees down to 0.00 cents.
